lines: Leather jokes need a <bold>thick skin</bold>. I keep saying that until someone laughs.
Leatherwork jokes need timing. Mine usually arrive with hide on them.
I keep a spare joke near the tannery. It is not always ready for public use.
I told a joke at the cauldron once. The workstation took it better than the villagers did.
Leatherworker jokes need good delivery and a strong finish.
I had a boot joke, but it walked away.
A stitch joke is small, tight, and easy to miss.
My belt joke holds up better than expected.
I told a dye joke once. It left a mark.
A saddle joke only works if everyone stays seated.
The tannery smell gets the first laugh and the last word.
I know a glove joke, but it needs handling carefully.
A strap pun can buckle under pressure.
My pouch joke has hidden depth and very little coin.
I asked the boot for feedback. It said I had sole.
The apron heard my best joke and remained stained but loyal.
A leather joke improves with age unless it dries out.
I tried a wet leather joke. It stretched too long.
The needle makes sharper points than I do.
